title_guess: NBFC registration with RBI, exemptions, and the types of NBFCs (by liability structure and by activity)
recurring_cast: piggy_bank labelled NBFC (the NBFC mascot, also beside the 'Different types of NBFCs' title)
brand_logo (RBI emblem coin with the letters RBI)
list_rail: a blue horizontal line with ten dots, type codes alternating above and below
blue pointer label that slides under one type at a time, with a yellow description box
running_examples: exemptions: a housing finance company (regulated by NHB), insurance companies (IRDA), stock brokers (SEBI) need not register with RBI
factoring story (voice only): company A sells goods to company B, holds an invoice, B pays after about two months; an NBFC factor pays A now, collects from B later, and keeps a fee as a discount
account aggregator story (voice only): FDs in one bank, mutual funds and stocks on two broking apps, a home loan from another bank, all seen on one dashboard (real brand names used)

best_moments.why: bank building and NBFC piggy bank face each other across a big 'VS': the recall of the previous video's comparison in one picture
the NBFC piggy sends a 'Register' arrow to the RBI coin, and an 'Exceptions' tag drops under the arrow: the rule and the fact that it has holes, before any list

a big '?' pops beside NBFC-ND exactly when the voice asks 'then where does their money come from?', and the answer line (markets and banks) appears under it later: the learner's question placed on the diagram
all ten activity types laid out at once on one rail, then a pointer walks along it: the learner sees the full set and where each item sits before each is explained

weak_moments.why: about 80 s on a nine-row English list of exempt companies and their regulators in small print; only a pointer arrow and a grey band move

the factoring story (company A, company B, invoice, two-month wait, NBFC pays now, collects later, fee as discount) runs about 65 s in voice only; the screen shows one text box and later a definition callout. This is exactly the scene BIE should draw
the account aggregator example (four accounts in four places, then one dashboard) is voice only and uses real bank and broker names; nothing is drawn
IFC lends directly while IDF buys debt securities: a two-route contrast said in voice, shown only as two text boxes at different times

check before reuse: the CIC-SI box says it gives long-term investment to core sectors (infrastructure, manufacturing, services); a core investment company is usually defined as one that holds mainly investments in its own group companies, so this looks wrong

check before reuse: housing finance companies are shown as regulated by NHB and exempt from RBI registration, yet NBFC-HFC is also one of the ten RBI types; HFC regulation is generally reported as moved to RBI in 2019, so the screen may be dated and is internally inconsistent. The RBI list usually also has NOFHC, which is missing
transcript gap about 75.5-90 s: the grey band over six exempt categories appears while the speech is not recognised

segments.teaches: NBFCs are classified two ways; by liability structure they are deposit-taking (NBFC-D, public can deposit) or non-deposit-taking (NBFC-ND, funded by markets and banks)

elements.what: 'Different types of NBFCs' with the piggy icon
CLASSIFICATION splits by green brackets into 'activities they undertake' and 'asset/liability structure'; the latter splits into NBFC-D and NBFC-ND
under NBFC-D: accept and hold public deposits
big '?' beside NBFC-ND
under NBFC-ND: source funding from markets and banks

segments.notes: 7 change events in 74 s. The '?' is timed to the voiced objection and stays until the answer.
segments.idea: some NBFCs take the public's deposits; the rest borrow from markets and banks
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to a title with the piggy; CLASSIFICATION forks by green brackets into two bases, and the liability side forks again into NBFC-D and NBFC-ND; a line under D says they hold public deposits; a big '?' pops beside ND as the question is asked, and the answer line (markets and banks) writes under it

segments.teaches: by activity there are ten types; NBFC-ICC offers loans, leasing, hire purchase and other credit; NBFC-IFC gives long-term loans to infrastructure; NBFC-IDF also funds infrastructure but by buying its debt securities

elements.what: subheading 'activities they undertake'

yellow description box under the label

segments.notes: 9 change events in 63 s. The IFC (direct loans) vs IDF (buys debt) contrast is spoken over the IDF label; only IDF's box carries it.
segments.idea: ten NBFC types by what they do; the first three finance credit and infrastructure
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to a blue rail that draws across with ten dots, codes alternating above and below; a blue pointer label slides under ICC with its full name and a yellow description box, then moves to IFC and IDF, each time swapping the name and box

segments.teaches: NBFC-MFI gives small loans to low-income people in rural and semi-urban areas for self-employment; NBFC-HFC lends to individuals and businesses to buy, build or renovate homes (small businesses often work from home); NBFC-MGC gives mortgage guarantees to banks, HFCs and other NBFCs
